notes: Product is discontinued and no longer listed on Teradek's live site (superseded by the MOTR-S / MOTR-S Max line); sourced via Wayback Machine capture of Teradek's own product page (SKU 15-0025, techSpecs2 JSON block), so it is authoritative manufacturer data even though not currently live — hence "medium" rather than "high" confidence. The motor has exactly one physical connector (no separate power jack); the motor cable itself is sold separately and not included. Other specs from the same source: operating voltage 7-17V DC, power draw <1W idle / 40W peak, operating temp -20C to 50C, max speed 3.0 rev/s, standard gear 0.8 Mod (0.4/0.5/0.6/0.8-wide also available), all-aluminum construction, dimensions 4.5 x 1.6 x 1 in (115 x 40 x 26 mm), weight 7.5 oz (212 g), mounts to 15/19mm rods. No bandwidth-graded ports present (not SDI/HDMI/DP/USB/Ethernet), so no grade was set. B&H Photo (bhphotovideo.com) confirms the same "4-Pin Hirose" connector convention on the related MK3.1 accessory cables (e.g. "RT MK3.1 Motor Cable," "4-Pin Hirose to D-Tap"), corroborating the connector type, though B&H no longer sells the motor itself as a standalone SKU (accessories only).

ports.name: Motor Connector (Power/Data)
ports.note: Real connector is a locking 4-pin Hirose (0B series, "1x 0B.4" per Teradek's own spec sheet), not a true XLR shell — chosen as the closest available connector id. Carries DC power (7–17V, <1W idle / 40W peak) from, and motor control/position data to and from, the MK3.1 Receiver via the separately-sold Motor Cable (11-1391).
